recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the R6 API-incubator move or its links need correction, address that as a separate current-scope issue rather than as FHIR-17178 follow-up.
issue_request: FHIR-17178 was Published/Persuasive and requested replacing the old DocumentReference generate named query, GET [service-url]/DocumentReference/?_query=generate..., with a formal DocumentReference $generate OperationDefinition that only supports POST because generating a resource can affect server state.
initial_application: The issue was applied for R5. Commit 3c56ef94e5 commented the old DocumentReference generate narrative as moved to a formal operation, and R5 history contains OperationDefinition/DocumentReference-generate with affectsState=true, code=generate, and a POST example. The old GET text remains only in an XHTML comment in documentreference-notes.xml.
additional_context: FHIR-34043 and FHIR-39624 later corrected the same $generate OperationDefinition parameters; both are already represented on the combined branch and current source reflects persist:boolean and return:Bundle. A later R6 commit, 3b38b80cf2, removed DocumentReference-generate from the core DocumentReference operation list and ballot-intro says DocumentReference.$generate moved out of this specification.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Re-adding DocumentReference-generate to the current core operation list would conflict with the later explicit move out of core, and deleting or editing the commented historical _query prose would not change the built specification.

evidence_items.summary: OperationDefinition.affectsState controls HTTP methods; operations generally use POST and GET is only required when affectsState=false and parameters are primitive.
evidence_items.learned: Setting DocumentReference-generate affectsState=true is the source-level mechanism that makes the operation POST-only under the general operations rules.
